label.description: The accessible name of the square, which is a role="group" holding two sliders. NOT optional: role="group" is in neither the accessibility lint's content-named roles nor its labelled ones, so an unnamed one is invisible to every gate, and a reader entering it is told they have entered a group and nothing more. "Colour" or the name of the property being edited is the right answer; the two axes carry their own names.

xLabel.description: The horizontal slider's accessible name. A prop rather than a constant because it is words on a screen reader's lips, and a shell in another language must be able to say them; the default is the English one so a consumer who does not care writes nothing.

yLabel.description: The vertical slider's accessible name, on the same terms as xLabel.

hue.description: The hue the square is drawn under, 0-360. The element READS it and never writes it: a saturation/brightness field has no hue of its own, and the control that owns the hue is a jx-color-slider beside it. Dragging into the grey corner therefore leaves the hue exactly where the reader put it, which is the whole reason the two are separate elements.

saturation.description: The horizontal axis, 0-100. It is the x coordinate of the thumb and the value of the horizontal range, and those are the same number rather than two that must be kept in step.

brightness.description: The vertical axis, 0-100, measured UPWARD from the bottom edge — 100 is the top. The thumb's CSS offset is the complement, computed in the document, because a reader's mental model of a colour square is bright at the top and a stylesheet's is zero at the top, and only one of those two should be in a prop.

step.description: The grid both axes move on, for the platform's own arrow keys, for the kit's cross-axis and ten-step keys, and for the snap a pointer drag is put through. One grid for the pointer and the keyboard is what stops the thumb and the announced value disagreeing during a drag.

disabled.description: Cannot be moved or focused. Forwarded to both ranges, so the refusal is the platform's; the pointer and key handlers check it too, because a pointer on the track never reaches a disabled control to be refused by it.

emits.name: input
emits.description: An axis is moving under the reader's hand. It comes from the ELEMENT, so e.target.saturation and e.target.brightness are the whole answer.

onInput.description: Mirrors whichever range moved into its axis and re-says input from the host. The native event is stopped: two controls holding half a coordinate each cannot both be e.target for one colour.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The reader committed a value; e.target is the element.

onChange.description: The same mirror and the same re-say, for the commit.

onKeydown.description: The two keyboard jobs a range cannot do for itself: the arrow across the OTHER axis, and Shift+Arrow for ten steps. An along-axis arrow with no Shift is left entirely to the platform, which already clamps, snaps and announces it.

onPointerDown.description: Takes the colour under the pointer, captures the gesture on the track, and puts the caret on the horizontal range so the keyboard carries on from where the pointer stopped. A single press with no movement is a complete gesture, which is what keeps this clear of WCAG 2.5.7.

onPointerMove.description: The drag. Nothing moves without a press first, so a hover across the square changes no colour.

onPointerUp.description: Ends the gesture and commits once. Bound to pointercancel as well as pointerup: a gesture the system takes away is over, and a square left in the dragging state would follow the next pointer that crossed it with no button down.

& > [part=\"track\"].background: linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, oklch(0 0 0)), linear-gradient(to right, oklch(1 0 0), var(--jx-color-area-hue))

& [part=\"x\"], & [part=\"y\"].$description: The two ranges are TRANSPARENT rather than hidden, and that is the whole accessibility of this element. display:none or visibility:hidden would take them out of the accessibility tree and out of the tab order, leaving a square only a pointer can operate — a WCAG 2.1.1 failure with a thumb drawn on it. opacity:0 keeps the role, the name, the announced value and the focus; pointer-events:none hands the gesture to the track, whose own handler owns the two-dimensional maths.
